evidence: Plaut. Asin. 270: quandō mēcum pariter pōtant, pariter scortārī solent
terms.comment: From scortum. Varro defines it: scortārī est saepius meretrīculam dūcere (LL 7.84, Lewis & Short). Ante- and post-classical.

phrases.latin: Nōn est flāgitium, mihi crēde, adulēscentulum scortārī neque pōtāre.
phrases.english: It is no outrage, believe me, for a young man to go whoring or drinking.

phrases.latin: nam sī istuc jūs est, senectā aetāte scortārī senēs, ubi locīst rēs summa nostra pūblica?
phrases.english: for if that is the rule, that old men go whoring in their old age, where does that leave our commonwealth?
